title: Dose Response Assay for Inducible Promoters in Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803
author: Anna Behle
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6tkhekw

steps.title: Inoculate BG11 with cyanobacteria
steps.instruction: Add the cyanobacterial strain to BG11 medium, include an empty‑vector control and appropriate antibiotics (to maintain plasmids). For a 6‑concentration, 3‑replicate design use 6 × 3 × 5 mL = 90 mL preculture; because the culture will be diluted ~1:3 before the assay, 35 mL culture volume is sufficient. Incubate 3–5 days until OD₇₅₀ ≈ 1.

steps.title: Dilute precultures to OD0.2
steps.instruction: Dilute the grown precultures with fresh BG11 (containing the same antibiotics) to an OD₇₅₀ of 0.2. Use only precultures that are ≤ 1 week old, not beyond early stationary phase, and whose OD₇₅₀ values are roughly equal.

steps.title: Grow precultures to OD0.6
steps.instruction: Continue incubating the OD₇₅₀ = 0.2 cultures for an additional 2–3 days until they reach an OD₇₅₀ of ≈ 0.6.

steps.title: Prepare main culture and aliquot to plates
steps.instruction: In a large sterile vessel dilute the OD₇₅₀ ≈ 0.6 culture to OD₇₅₀ = 0.2 (maintaining antibiotics). Aliquot 5 mL of this main culture into each well of clear 6‑well plates, ensuring at least three biological replicates for every inducer concentration.

steps.title: Add equal inducer volumes to replicates
steps.instruction: For each well add inducer so that the total added volume is identical across all replicates. This can be done by (a) preparing a separate stock solution for each desired inducer concentration, or (b) adding solvent to wells receiving lower inducer amounts to match the total volume.

substeps.instruction: Prepare individual inducer stock solutions covering the required concentration range (tables for promoters P_rha, P_L03, P_vanCC are provided in the original document).
Add the calculated volume of each stock to the corresponding wells.
Add sterile solvent to wells receiving less inducer so that every well receives the same final volume.

steps.title: Measure fluorescence and cell density
steps.instruction: At 6 h, 24 h, and 48 h post‑induction, transfer 150 µL from each well into a black‑walled, clear‑bottom 96‑well plate in technical triplicates; include a BG11 blank well. Shake the plate at 500 rpm for 30 s (double orbital) before reading. Record fluorescence on a BMG Clariostar using top‑optic mode, excitation 511 ± 6 nm, emission 552 ± 10 nm, with 20 flashes per well. Measure absorbance at 750 nm to quantify cell density.
